subtitle: "Computational methods for nanopore measurements"

Finite-element simulations and event-level analysis support the interpretation of nanopore measurements and comparisons across device architectures.

## Research question

How can modeling and data analysis connect heterogeneous nanopore structure with electric fields, transport behavior, and measured signals?

## Approach and contributions

I used COMSOL simulations to investigate electric-field distributions and transport behavior in heterogeneous nanopores. Quantitative signal analysis and event-feature extraction support statistical comparisons and machine-learning classification of experimental signals.

In this research, I developed structural-classification approaches that achieved **more than 96% classification accuracy** on the experimental signals studied. This result describes the specific research analysis; performance on other devices or datasets requires separate evaluation.

## Related work

[Multilayer heterostructure research](heterostructures.qmd) connects these methods with device fabrication and directional transport. [Research presentations](../talks-news.qmd#research-presentations) include my work on machine-learning-enabled nanopore biosensing.
